facts.text: Jinshan Temple (Jiangtian Chan Temple) was founded in the Eastern Jin dynasty, over 1,600 years ago, and is one of the four great Chan temples of China.
The temple is built up the hillside of the Jinshan scenic area, crowned by the Cishou Pagoda; Zhongling Spring and the Bailong Cave are in the same area.
It is the setting of the White Snake legend, in which the white snake spirit floods the monastery.
Paddle and electric boats can be taken on the lake.

facts.text: Jiaoshan is the only island in the Yangtze that visitors can tour; surrounded by water on all sides, a national 5A scenic area.
Dinghui Temple (originally Puji Chan Temple) lies hidden in a fold of the hill, and the Jiaoshan Stele Forest holds over 400 stone tablets, including the Yihe Ming inscription.
Iron cannons from the 1842 defence against British forces can still be found on the island.
Reached by boat; the last ferry off the island leaves 17:00-18:00 depending on season.

facts.text: Xijindu is an ancient Yangtze ferry crossing at the foot of Yuntai Mountain; the street is under 500 m long and has kept buildings from Tang to Qing.
Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda (Yuan dynasty) and the Former British Consulate stand on the street, both national protected sites.
It won UNESCO's Asia-Pacific heritage conservation award in 2001 and is a national 4A scenic area and national tourism and leisure street.
Heavily restored, with shops and restaurants aimed at tourists.

facts.text: Beigu Hill is on the Yangtze's south bank, about 58 m high, named 'north solid' for its steep, defensible cliffs.
Ganlu Temple on the summit is traditionally where Liu Bei came to marry, the story behind the opera Longfeng Chengxiang.
From the top you can see Jiaoshan to the east and Jinshan to the west; a 'Number One River and Mountain Under Heaven' inscription is on the slope.
An iron pagoda (Weigong Pagoda, rebuilt several times, lower base Song dynasty) stands near Qinghui Pavilion.

facts.text: Zhenjiang Museum was founded in 1958 in the former British Consulate buildings on Yuntai Mountain, at 85 Boxian Road.
Collections include Wu-state bronzes, Six Dynasties celadon, Tang gold and silver, Song silks and Jingjiang school paintings.
General admission is free.

zhenjiang-5.notes: DUPLICATE WARNING: zhenjiang-5 (Zhenjiang Museum) and zhenjiang-6 (Former British Consulate) are the same site: the museum occupies the consulate buildings (zh Wikipedia, China Daily), pins 60 m apart. Suggest merging or dropping one. The museum also runs the Pearl S. Buck residence, Lu Xiaobo residence and Mengxi Garden per zh Wikipedia (as of May 2024). No en Wikipedia article.

facts.text: Britain built the consulate on Yuntai Mountain in 1864; it was burned in 1888 riots and rebuilt in 1889-90 on 17 mu.
Five colonial-veranda buildings (office, chief and vice consul residences, staff quarters, club) are set into the hillside.
A national key heritage site, it has housed Zhenjiang Museum since 1958.

zhenjiang-6.ticketUrl_evidence: Housed in Zhenjiang Museum; no separate site.
zhenjiang-6.notes: Same site as zhenjiang-5 (the museum is the consulate); free because the museum is free. A 2025 visitor review (via Ctrip search result) says the consulate can only be viewed from the door. Recommend merge or drop as near-duplicate.

facts.text: Nanshan Scenic Area is a national 4A scenic area and national forest park south of the city, taking in 21 hills including Zhaoyin, Huanghe and Jia.
On Zhaoyin Mountain Prince Zhaoming compiled the Wen Xuan anthology at Zhaoyin Temple; the area also has Helin Temple, Zhulin Temple and several springs.
A large pagoda on the hilltop gives views over the city and river; the climb takes under an hour.

zhenjiang-7.notes: Operator ticket notice: Nanshan adult 30 low / 40 high season, same-day, covers Wenyuan, Zhulin and Zhaoyin sites. Not in any park pass. No en Wikipedia article.

facts.text: Zhulin ('Bamboo Forest') Temple sits in a valley between two hills near Zhaoyin Mountain, so ringed by bamboo it cannot be seen from afar.
The temple is built on Jia Hill; stone steps climb five terraces of bamboo and old trees.
Zhulin is one of the three sites covered by the Nanshan ticket.

facts.text: Zhenjiang Vinegar Culture Museum opened in 2010, built by Hengshun Group, in the city famous for Zhenjiang vinegar; a national 4A attraction.
It documents the history of vinegar, with a recreated ancient vinegar workshop and the modern production process.
It covers 4,000 square metres.

facts.text: The residence stands at the top of Dengyun Mountain in western Zhenjiang, built in the early 20th century, and is now a cultural park with the residence, a memorial hall and a bookhouse.
It is one of the sites run by Zhenjiang Museum.
Pearl S. Buck won the Pulitzer Prize for The Good Earth and the 1938 Nobel Prize in Literature; she lived in Zhenjiang as a child.

facts.text: Mount Mao (Maoshan) is a Taoist holy mountain, 372 m at its highest, on the Jurong-Jintan boundary; the climb takes about an hour.
It is the birthplace of the Shangqing school of Taoism, called the 'Eighth Cave Heaven and First Blessed Land'.
It was also one of the bases during the Anti-Japanese War.
